items.title: Boy, 11, dies after being shot with homemade gun in Keningau
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: An 11-year-old boy died from a gunshot wound to the head after being shot with a homemade firearm known as a 'Ginsok' in Kampung Mampulut, Sook, Keningau, last Saturday. Keningau police chief Superintendent Erwansyah Abdul Basir said police received a report about the incident, which occurred at a rubber smallholding hut, at 2.35pm. He said the victim was taken to Keningau Hospital but was pronounced dead.

items.title: Malaysia should focus on tax revenue collection, not SST vs GST – Expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's tax debate should focus on enhancing revenue collection rather than choosing between the Sales and Service Tax (SST) and the Goods and Services Tax (GST), said an expert. KPMG Malaysia senior advisor on tax policy Dr Veerinderjeet Singh said Malaysia already has the relevant taxes in place, with the key challenge being to ensure they perform effectively and deliver the intended revenue. "We have already crossed the tax invoicing element.

items.title: Heavy rain triggers slope collapse, damages house in Kundasang
items.summary: KUNDASANG: A slope collapse measuring about 25 metres high, triggered by continuous heavy rain, damaged the rear wall of a house in Kampung Pogun and Kampung Dumpiring Atas here yesterday. APM said preliminary inspections found that the slope collapse was caused by continuous heavy rain in the area. Continuous heavy rain since yesterday evening had also triggered landslides and flash floods in several areas around Kundasang.

items.title: Pahang closes schools in Kuantan, Rompin as haze worsens
items.summary: KUANTAN: Schools in Kuantan and Rompin will be closed tomorrow due to worsening haze, the Pahang Education Department said. In a statement, the department said all educational institutions under its jurisdiction in the two districts would be temporarily closed from Oct 13, pending further instructions, following the haze and prevailing Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. The department said educational institutions in both districts had been instructed to minimise activities that could expose students and the education community to unhealthy air.

items.title: Malaysia targets 3.3pc fiscal deficit in 2027, 3pc by 2028, says Treasury sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Malaysia is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.3 per cent next year as it presses ahead with plans to bring the figure down to 3 per cent by 2028, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said today. Speaking at a panel discussion titled “Post-Budget 2027 Debate” organised by the Malaysian Economic Association in Kuala Lumpur, Johan said fiscal consolidation remained a key government priority, particularly in maintaining investor confidence. The government is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.6 per cent this year, after reducing it from 5.5 per cent in 2022 to 3.7 per cent in 2025.

items.title: MN Holdings bags RM293.9 mln data centre infrastructure contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary MN Power Transmission Sdn Bhd has secured a total contract value of RM293.88 million for the construction of two 275 kilovolt (kV) consumer landing stations (CLSs) for a data centre development located in the central region of Peninsular Malaysia. MN Holdings executive director Datuk Dang Siong Diang said the project demonstrates the continued demand for high-voltage power infrastructure to support large-scale data centre developments. "We remain focused on executing these projects effectively while continuing to pursue opportunities across the power infrastructure, data centre and utilities sectors across Peninsular Malaysia," he said.

items.title: Kedah teen held captive, tortured for two days before being killed
items.summary: Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said police were alerted to the discovery of the dead body at 8.05am on Thursday. Adzli said police arrested 14 men, aged between 16 and 24, in Gurun and Guar Chempedak between noon and 10.30pm on the same day. He said 12 suspects had been remanded for six days until Wednesday, while two underage suspects were remanded for five days until tomorrow to facilitate investigations.

items.title: 2027 power subsidy plan under review: Treasury sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is reviewing the electricity subsidy mechanism for 2027 with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and the Energy Commission. Johan said the current mechanism, which runs until Dec 31, aims to protect about 85 per cent of households from higher electricity bills. This resulted in significantly higher electricity bills for affected consumers, prompting the government to review the level of protection.

items.title: Johor mosques, surau to hold solat hajat until haze improves
items.summary: State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the solat hajat initiative was aimed at seeking divine intervention for the haze to subside and air quality to improve. The initiative comes as seven of Johor's eight air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Pasir Gudang recording the highest at 174. Fared expressed hope that the collective prayers would contribute to the well-being of Johoreans as the state awaits an improvement in air quality.

items.title: Seven-year-old seriously injured in Johor stray dog attack, teen escapes unhurt in earlier incident at same location
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 12 — A seven-year-old boy suffered serious injuries after he was attacked by eight stray dogs while playing at a playground at a housing complex in Lima Kedai here today. Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad expressed concern over the incident urging authorities to address the issue of stray dogs. Pandak said the incident involving the child was the second to occur today.

items.title: 100 students advance to final round of MRSM Bintang Media 2026 challenge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 100 students from 42 Mara Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) nationwide advanced to the final round of MRSM Bintang Media 2026 held at Balai Berita, Bangsar, today. MRSM Bintang Media 2026, held as part of the 'Siri Jelajah MRSM' and Media Prima Talent Development Programme, aimed to give students first-hand exposure to the media industry by learning directly from experienced media practitioners. The programme featured four categories — Journalism and News Writing by Berita Harian (BH), The Art of Writing and News Journalism by New Straits Times (NST), Broadcasting and News Presentation, and Photojournalism and Visual Storytelling.

items.title: Budget must fire up corporate growth: CGS International CEO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Corporate Malaysia should leverage the 2027 Budget to accelerate investment, improve productivity and build more sustainable and internationally competitive businesses amid rising global uncertainties. CGS International Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Khairi Shahrin Arief Baki said the fifth Madani Budget offered businesses opportunities to strengthen resilience through technology adoption, workforce development, sustainability and increased productive capacity. Malaysia needs both, rising together," he said.

items.title: Lee Lam Thye: Workplace sustainability must put workers' safety, health first
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Workplace sustainability must prioritise workers' safety, health and dignity, with stronger governance and accountability needed to prevent accidents and protect lives, said Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye. Lee said workplace sustainability must go beyond environmental protection, energy conservation and technological advancement to include physical safety, mental well-being and work environments designed around human needs. "A safe workplace begins with good governance, and good governance begins with leadership and accountability," he said.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 12, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia continued last week's positive performance, led by bargain hunting in banking stocks as Budget 2027 offered additional support through measures targeting small and medium enterprises (SMEs) lending, housing financing and investment-driven credit growth. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin rose to approximately RM340,435. Following the trend, Ethereum traded higher at approximately RM10,405, while Solana stood at approximately RM454.78.

items.title: Minimum-wage exemption apt for MSMEs to ease cost pressure: Samenta
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from the RM2,000 minimum wage requirement is necessary to ease cost pressures and preserve their capacity to invest, automate and expand. Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) president Datuk William Ng said businesses had faced mounting cost pressures over the past two years, even before the latest energy crisis, squeezing profit margins despite higher sales. Ng said the association supported the government's decision to exempt MSMEs from the latest minimum wage increase, as higher labour costs could further strain businesses already facing tight margins.

items.title: Teacher accused of forcing pupils to perform oral sex during home tuition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A teacher has been accused of sexually abusing several male pupils, including forcing them to perform oral sex during tuition classes at his home in Bukit Jalil over the past few months. The teacher, who works at a school in Bukit Jalil, held tuition classes at his residence for pupils, including those attending the school where he teaches. A source said several parents lodged police reports yesterday after learning about the incidents.

items.title: Govt aims to improve water quality in 33 polluted rivers in Malaysia by 10pc, says DPM Fadillah
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the target was set at the second 2026 meeting of the National Special Committee on Addressing River Water Quality Deterioration, which he chaired today. In Selangor, the Selangor Water Management Authority (Luas) reported 144 cases of water source pollution detected over the three years up to September 14, 2026, with varying levels of risk. Fadillah said polluted rivers could disrupt water treatment plant operations, affect public water supplies, increase treatment costs and affect economic activities, underscoring the need to make water resource protection a shared priority at all levels of administration.

items.title: 'We feel threatened until he is punished,' says stabbed nurse's daughter
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The daughter of a nurse who was stabbed by her husband attended the Sessions Court here today to follow proceedings involving her stepfather, whom she believes is not mentally ill. Nik Ruziany Nik Ahmad Ruzi, 19, said she was determined to be present to hear the charges against her 44-year-old stepfather, whom she described as cruel for stabbing her mother. "Today I am here with several family members, although my heart hurts to see my stepfather, who treated my mother in a way that left her hospitalised. She said the family would not feel safe until her stepfather was given an appropriate sentence.

items.title: Budget 2027: Pet vaccination, sterilisation eligible for tax relief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The government proposes expanding the scope of individual income tax relief for lifestyle to include pet care expenses, such as vaccinations and sterilisation treatments by registered veterinary services. MoF said the personal income tax relief cap for lifestyle remains at RM2,500, including the proposed expansion. Additionally, to promote digital literacy and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technology to boost productivity and drive innovation, the scope of the personal income tax relief for lifestyle is proposed to be expanded to include subscription costs for AI software and applications for personal use, spouses, or children.

items.title: High Court allows MCMC’s preliminary objection, Papagomo committal hearing on Dec 23
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The High Court will first hear the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) committal application against blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, before proceeding with the inter-partes injunction hearing. “The court also extended the existing ad interim injunction against Wan Muhammad Azri until December 23. Therefore, MCMC has applied to the court for leave to commence a committal proceeding against Wan Azri.

items.title: Opposition proposes renaming Putrajaya Hospital after Dr Siti Hasmah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin has backed a proposal to rename Putrajaya Hospital after the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali in recognition of her contributions to the country's healthcare system. Hamzah (PN-Larut) was responding to a proposal by Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah) to name the hospital after the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad. Mas Ermieyati said the move would be a fitting tribute to Dr Siti Hasmah.

items.title: Malaysia, Jordan seek high-tech cooperation to train more engineers, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Malaysia and Jordan are seeking to expand strategic cooperation in high-tech industries, particularly semiconductors and advanced technical education and training, to develop more engineers and skilled workers for future industry needs. “We also discussed potential cooperation in developing advanced technical education and training centres, including producing more engineers and skilled workers to meet future industry demands,” he posted on Facebook. Anwar said discussions also covered expanding trade and investment, including a potential free trade agreement (FTA), tariff restructuring, stronger supply chains and cooperation in energy, transport, the halal industry and tourism.

items.title: Viral image of crocodile near Seberang Jaya Hospital being probed
items.summary: SEBERANG JAYA: An image purportedly showing a crocodile in a drain outside Seberang Jaya Hospital has gone viral, prompting calls for an investigation into its authenticity. Seberang Jaya assemblyman Izhar Shah Arif Shah said he had alerted the Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) and the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) after receiving the information. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: IJM Corporation bags RM1.23 bln contruction contract for AT&S facilities in Kedah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IJM Corporation Bhd's wholly-owned subsidiary, IJM Construction Sdn Bhd, has accepted a letter of award from AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd for a design and build contract worth about RM1.23 billion. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the contract involves the construction of a four-storey production facility, a three-storey central utility building and a single-storey wastewater treatment facility at Kulim Hi-Tech Park, Kedah. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Iswami calls for stronger regional action on haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ikatan Setiakawan Wartawan Malaysia-Indonesia (Iswami) Malaysia has called for stronger regional cooperation to address transboundary haze caused by forest and land fires in Indonesia. He said Iswami Malaysia had outlined five priorities, including protecting public health through air quality monitoring, accurate information, health advice and protective measures for vulnerable groups. Zaini called for Malaysia and Indonesia to share hotspot data, smoke movement monitoring, information and technical assistance, and coordinate firefighting operations when necessary.

items.title: Immigration Dept to intensify crackdown on illegal foreign workers, employers in Janda Baik
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department will intensify enforcement operations in Janda Baik, Pahang, following concerns raised by residents over the growing presence of foreigners and their involvement in economic activities in the area. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department was taking the concerns seriously, particularly over the possibility of illegal employment and accommodation arrangements involving undocumented foreigners. He said enforcement efforts would not only target undocumented migrants but also employers, business operators and property owners found employing, harbouring or allowing them to stay on their premises.

items.title: Tok Mat: Malaysians advised to postpone Umrah trips amid security concerns
items.summary: SEPANG: Malaysians are advised to temporarily postpone travel to Saudi Arabia for umrah following security concerns after a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. Yesterday, the Foreign Ministry reported that no Malaysians had been killed or injured in Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh or the incident involving a projectile that fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that the attack on King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and injured 309 others.

items.title: Growth must lift living standards: Johan Merican
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's strong economic performance must translate into tangible improvements in living standards as the government balances economic growth with fiscal consolidation under the 2027 Budget. Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Merican said Malaysia had recorded encouraging economic growth, but the gains had yet to fully translate into public satisfaction with the economy. Malaysia's economy grew 5.2 per cent in 2025, while the government has projected growth of between 4.8 and 5.3 per cent this year, before moderating to between 4.2 and 5.2 per cent in 2027.

items.title: TNB confirms electrical accident at its installation in Johor’s Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) has confirmed an electrical accident involving a member of the public at one of its installations in Kota Tinggi, Johor, today. In a statement posted on Facebook by TNB CareLine, the utility company said its technical team was dispatched to the location shortly after receiving a report of the incident. The company also advised the public against tampering with, opening or approaching electrical installations, warning that such actions could result in serious injury or death.

items.title: Zaliha proposes gender-responsive budget statement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Finance Ministry should prepare a Gender Responsive Budget Statement detailing how public spending benefits women and identifying gaps in policies affecting them, said Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa. Zaliha, who is Government Backbenchers Club (BBC) chairman, said the statement should detail allocations, beneficiary groups, targets and policy outcomes by gender, beginning with the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry before being extended to other ministries. "I would like to propose that the Finance Ministry consider preparing a Gender Responsive Budget Statement detailing allocations, beneficiary groups, targets and policy outcomes according to gender.

items.title: Banks ease loan repayment concerns for families of missing Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Banks have given interim assurances that they will not pressure families of 54 Malaysians missing after floods in Nepal, Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope said. Its coordinator and spokesperson, Dr R. Manivannan, said the assurance followed a two-and-a-half-hour meeting at Bank Negara Malaysia involving financial institutions, insurance companies and the missing Malaysians' next of kin. He said the families needed a clear, coordinated solution to their loved ones' outstanding financial commitments.

items.title: No need to replace old birth certificates, still valid, says NRD; new copies cost RM5
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 12 — Old birth certificates, including handwritten documents issued in paper format, remain valid and do not need to be replaced, said National Registration Department (NRD) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias. Badrul Hisham said birth documentation was essential to establish a legally recognised identity and ensure individuals could access their rights and services as Malaysians. He said the NRD continued to reach out to communities, including the Orang Asli in rural areas, to ensure they had access to registration and documentation services.

items.title: Rain fails to clear Johor haze as seven areas record unhealthy air
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Rainfall has failed to bring widespread relief from the haze in Johor, with seven of the state's eight air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy readings today. The latest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings showed Pasir Gudang recording the highest level at 174, followed by Kota Tinggi (170) and Pengerang (166). Segamat was the only district to record moderate air quality, with an API reading of 95.

items.title: Kedah police bust online scam syndicate posing as Indian police officers
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 12 — Kedah police successfully crippled an online scam syndicate involving suspects posing as Indian police officers during a raid on a business premises in Bandar Putra, Kulim, last Friday. Kedah Police Chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said that during the joint operation at 8pm, police arrested 48 individuals suspected of acting as syndicate members, comprising seven locals, eight Indian nationals, and 33 Pakistani nationals. “Additionally, police seized various items including 89 mobile phones, seven laptops, modems, monitors, Indian police uniforms, Indian flags, Indian Central Bureau of Investigation flags, and several other items.

items.title: Bank Negara, financial industry ready to support Nepal victims' families
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia and financial institutions are ready to provide relief and support to families of Malaysians missing after the Nepal-China floods, subject to applicable laws and regulatory requirements. "Bank Negara and the financial industry representatives reiterated readiness to extend appropriate relief and support to the families of the victims affected by this tragedy, in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements," Bank Negara said in a statement. The meeting involved 44 next of kin and representatives from financial industry associations and financial service providers.

items.title: Schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Putrajaya closed tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan and Putrajaya will be closed tomorrow due to the haze, said Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek. In a notice posted on social media, Fadhlina said the closure on Oct 13 would also cover schools under the Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat and Sepang District Education Offices (PPD) in Selangor, as well as the Kuantan and Rompin PPDs in Pahang. "Schools in Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis, Penang, Perak, Terengganu, Sabah and Sarawak will operate as usual," she said.

items.title: KLIA to conduct full-scale emergency exercise on Wednesday — MAHB
items.summary: SEPANG: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) will conduct a full-scale emergency exercise, Ex Perisai Panthera 2026, on Runway 2 on Oct 14. Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said in a statement today that the exercise, scheduled from 8 am to 2 pm, was part of KLIA's ongoing efforts to strengthen its emergency preparedness. — BERNAMA TAGS: MAHB, exercise, KLIA, aviation, safety © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: 1MDB in settlement talks with Deutsche Bank
items.summary: 1MDB's counsel, Datuk Lim Chee Wee, informed the Federal Court of the settlement talks during proceedings today before a three-member panel led by Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah. The panel, comprising Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Seri Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru, was hearing 1MDB's application for leave to appeal against a decision in favour of UK law firm White & Case LLP. The hearing for that case is scheduled for Oct 26 before High Court Judicial Commissioner Rihada Rafie," Lim said.

items.title: Two killed, two injured in three-vehicle pile-up on Federal Highway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Two men were killed while two others were injured in an accident involving three cars at Kilometer 18.2 of the Federal Highway heading towards Kuala Lumpur, early this morning. Petaling Jaya District Police Chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said the accident, which occurred at approximately 12.20am, involved a Proton Wira driven by a local man in his 20s who was travelling from Shah Alam to Kuala Lumpur. Shamsudin said the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters received a report regarding the fatal accident at 1:05 am today.

items.title: Opposition leader criticises GLC involvement in non-core projects in Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that government-linked corporations (GLCs) were being made to operate beyond their core mandates. While debating Budget 2027, he cited a project to build a hostel for students that he said would be funded by the Retirement Fund Incorporated (KWAP), alleging this practice extended to others such as Petronas, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and more. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for 2027 last Friday, in which he also outlined a RM50 billion from government-linked investment companies, state enterprises and statutory bodies.

items.title: Johor fisheries seize banned dragon traps worth RM42,600
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor Fisheries Department seized 356 banned dragon traps and other fishing equipment worth RM42,600 in an enforcement operation off Muar and Batu Pahat. The seized equipment comprised 356 dragon traps, five stingray nets and a mini trawl net. Rosmawati said dragon traps and stingray nets were prohibited under the Fisheries (Prohibition of Fishing Methods) (Amendment) Regulations 2024.

items.title: 1MDB in talks to settle lawsuit with Deutsche Bank
items.summary: 1MDB’s counsel, Datuk Lim Chee Wee, informed the Federal Court of the settlement talks during proceedings today before a three-member panel led by Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah. The panel, comprising Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Seri Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru, was hearing 1MDB’s application for leave to appeal against a decision in favour of UK law firm White & Case LLP. The hearing for that case is scheduled for October 26 before High Court Judicial Commissioner Rihada Rafie,” Lim said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan ruler to skip Conference of Rulers meeting, palace says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, will not attend the Conference of Rulers meeting scheduled from October 13 to 15, the Negeri Sembilan Palace said today. In a statement, Royal Comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said attendance at the Conference of Rulers meeting did not require an invitation. He also clarified that Tuanku Muhriz had not received any letter or formal invitation from the meeting’s chairman, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah, to attend the pre-council meeting.

items.title: High Court jails construction worker three years for Palestinian abduction tied to hacking secrets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — A construction worker who was previously charged with kidnapping a Palestinian man was sentenced to three years in prison by the High Court here today for abducting and confining the man at a chalet four years ago. Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin imposed the sentence on Edy Ko’im Said, 46, after he pleaded guilty to an alternative charge of abducting and confining the Palestinian man. The court ordered the father of three to begin serving his prison sentence today.

items.title: Batik Air: Flight OD701 from KLIA to Jeddah called off as precautionary measure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Batik Air has cancelled its scheduled flight from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, today as a precautionary measure amid the ongoing conflict. “The affected flight, OD701, was scheduled to depart Kuala Lumpur for King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah at 7.25pm. Passengers were also advised to check Batik Air’s official website and social media channels for the latest flight updates.

items.title: Haze worsens: 23 stations record ‘Unhealthy’ API levels across Malaysia
items.summary: No station recorded very unhealthy or hazardous levels. Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded the highest reading at 174, followed by Kota Tinggi, also in Johor, at 170. Johor had seven stations in the unhealthy range.

items.title: Kuraman Island sand spit stretches into record books, spurring Labuan’s ecotourism appeal
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 12 — The natural sand spit on Kuraman Island has set two national records in the Malaysia Book of Records (MBR), with its total length measuring 808.4 metres and its exposed section measuring 790.4 metres. The two records are ‘Longest Natural Sand Spit in Malaysia’ (Beting Pasir Semula Jadi Terpanjang di Malaysia) and ‘Longest Exposed Sand Spit in Malaysia’ (Beting Pasir Terdedah Terpanjang di Malaysia). Muhammad Azmi said the recognition marked a significant milestone in efforts to promote Labuan’s geological heritage and tourism potential, while raising the profile of Kuraman Island and Labuan Geopark nationally.

items.title: Fadhlina: Schools closed tomorrow in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Putrajaya as haze worsens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Schools across Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, and Putrajaya, as well as several districts in Selangor and Pahang, will be closed tomorrow following a sharp deterioration in air quality, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek announced today. The mandatory closures also extend to schools under four District Education Offices (PPD) in Selangor: Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat, and Sepang. In Pahang, schools under PPD Kuantan and PPD Rompin will likewise remain closed.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh says DBKL, police mull joint control centre for KL’s 10,000 CCTVs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) are considering establishing a control centre to give the police better access to the closed-circuit television (CCTV) system across the federal capital. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the initiative is crucial as about 10,000 CCTV units are installed throughout Kuala Lumpur. Sentul police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the ICT system will significantly help speed up services to the public, especially when lodging police reports.

items.title: Education minister: Decisions on school haze closures guided by MetMalaysia, Health Ministry and NRES
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Decisions regarding the closure and reopening of schools due to the haze situation will be made periodically based on standard operating procedures (SOPs), existing guidelines, and advice from relevant agencies. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said these decisions depend on advice of the Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) and the Ministry of Health (MOH), as well as the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES). Fadhlina said the current haze situation is being monitored according to established guidelines, however, parents must continue to prioritise their children’s health.

items.title: High Court fixes June 14, 2027 for Bar bid to revive Zahid graft case
items.summary: Judge S. Indra Nehru set the date after lawyer Abhilaash Subramaniam, representing the Malaysian Bar, informed the court that Ahmad Zahid and the Attorney-General (AG) had obtained leave from the Federal Court on Oct 8 to appeal against an earlier Court of Appeal ruling. “We therefore request that the judicial review hearing at the High Court be held after the Federal Court appeal proceedings are concluded,” Abhilaash said during case management. The court also directed that the next case management be conducted via e-review before a High Court deputy registrar.

items.title: Opposition leader challenges Putrajaya to revive GST, end ‘uncertainty’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that the government’s hybrid taxation proposal was tacit admission that it was wrong to reject the goods and services tax (GST). While debating the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027, Hamzah said recent proposals to incorporate elements of the consumption tax into the existing Sales and Service Tax (SST) also indicated that the latter system was lacking. “If you want the GST, just implement the GST.

items.title: Malaysia urges Umrah pilgrims to hold off travel after deadly Riyadh airport missile strike
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 12 — Malaysians are advised to temporarily postpone travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah following security concerns after a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. “There has been no incident in Makkah, but the missile explosion in Riyadh has raised security concerns,” he told reporters after attending the departure of Jordan’s King Abdullah II at the Bunga Raya Complex here today Yesterday, the Foreign Ministry reported that no Malaysians had been killed or injured in Saturday’s attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh or the incident involving a projectile that fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that the attack on King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and injured 309 others.

items.title: Heavy rain, gusty winds expected across nine states, Putrajaya and Labuan until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across multiple states, forecasting heavy rain, lightning, and gusty winds in parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, Sabah, and the Federal Territory of Labuan until 6pm today. In the northern and eastern regions of the peninsula, the warning encompasses Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, and Selama), Kelantan (Jeli and Gua Musang), and Terengganu (Dungun, Hulu Terengganu, and Kemaman). In Negeri Sembilan, stormy weather is expected across Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau, and Kuala Pilah.

items.title: Man found electrocuted beside Kota Tinggi TNB substation, cable theft attempt suspected
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 12 — An unidentified man was found dead early this morning, believed to have been electrocuted while attempting to steal power cables near a Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) substation in Felda Adela, near Sungai Rengit. Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said law enforcement was alerted after receiving an emergency call through the MERS 999 response system at 6.46am regarding an unconscious individual. “Following the information, a police team from the Kota Tinggi district police headquarters were immediately despatched to the scene to investigate.

items.title: From Jan 2027, only JPJ‑approved intermediaries can handle customer transactions at counters nationwide
items.summary: ARAU, Oct 12 — Only individuals or company representatives registered as intermediaries and approved by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) will be allowed to conduct transactions on behalf of customers at all JPJ offices and branches nationwide from January 1. JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the requirement was aimed at regulating intermediary services more systematically, transparently and with integrity. Aedy Fadly said the implementation did not mean that JPJ had any ties, cooperation or business relationship with any registered intermediary.

items.title: Sarawak announces 25pc electricity bill discount for 716,000 households under 2027 budget
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 12 — The Sarawak government today announced a 25 per cent discount on electricity bills from January to December next year under the 2027 State Budget. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg, when tabling the budget at the State Legislative Assembly today, said the discount would benefit about 716,000 domestic consumers across Sarawak, at a cost of RM281 million. The state government also announced a RM5 monthly subsidy for water bills under the free water programme, benefiting about 600,000 domestic consumers, at RM35 million.

items.title: Opposition proposes national entity to manage RM800b rare earth wealth, prevent illegal mining losses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The opposition has proposed the establishment of a national entity to manage rare earth elements (REE) as a new source of national wealth in the post-petroleum era. Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said the entity was necessary to prevent non-radioactive raw materials worth more than RM800 billion from being sold cheaply without value-added processing or lost through illegal mining activities. He also said Malaysia needed to move beyond merely selling cheap electricity to foreign data centres and instead become an Asean energy powerhouse by exporting clean energy, owning regional grid infrastructure and developing energy technology.

items.title: Home Ministry developing AI‑based National Border Control System to strengthen surveillance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Home Ministry is developing an artificial intelligence (AI)-based National Border Control System (SKSN) incorporating data analytics to strengthen surveillance and security enforcement along Malaysia’s borders. Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the system would serve as a smart surveillance platform, enabling real-time information sharing among enforcement agencies, detecting suspicious movement patterns and expediting responses in high-risk areas. “Through SKSN, intelligence and surveillance systems will be integrated.

items.title: Mother agrees bruising on Zara Qairina’s back caused by blood clotting, not a blow
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 12 — The mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir agreed with the medical expert’s explanation at the Coroner’s Court here today that the bruising on her daughter’s back observed while bathing the body was not caused by a blow, but rather by blood clotting. Noraidah Lamat, 46, the 82nd witness in the inquest proceedings, said she was informed of this by a doctor on August 10 last year, after she had voiced concerns that the bruising might have resulted from being struck by a blunt object. When asked by lawyer Abdul Fikry Jaafar Abdullah whether the bruising was indeed due to blood clotting as explained by the doctor rather than a blow, Noraidah replied: “That is correct, sir.”
